method: Lab revenue = U.S. white-collar wage bill × share of that work AI can do × share of that work AI actually does × labs' share of its value. The wage bill is the covered occupations' employment times mean wage (BLS OEWS, May 2025), held at that level so dollars stay comparable. The share AI can do is this site's index, weighted by wages: its two forecasts, then its trend.

The work AI actually does today comes from the St. Louis Fed's Real-Time Population Survey: the share of work hours that workers say generative AI saved them, by occupation group, weighted by this site's wage bill. Divided by what AI can do, it gives today's adoption. It is projected on an S-curve: it grows at the scenario's first-year rate and slows as it nears the scenario's peak.
The labs' share of the value

Today's share is lab revenue divided by the pay for the work AI does. It comes out high, about two-thirds, partly because revenue is global and includes consumer subscriptions while the work is U.S. white-collar, and partly because the survey counts only hours that workers save themselves: it misses work agents take on without a worker in the loop and extra output in the same hours. Read it as an upper bound.

As adoption grows, the share moves to the scenario's long-run value, reaching it at peak adoption. A long-run share of 25% means each dollar of pay for work AI does earns the labs about 25 cents a year; the rest stays with customers as savings, with the software built on the models, and in lower prices as labs compete. It is an assumption, not a measurement; the sliders let you set your own.

Lab revenue is global, while the wage bill is U.S. white-collar pay, so the ratio is a yardstick for scale rather than a claim that the revenue replaces U.S. wages. About 72% of Anthropic's revenue is billed to U.S. addresses (S-1); OpenAI does not disclose a split; its revenue was about 60% consumer at the start of 2026 and mostly enterprise by August.

Anthropic books cloud-marketplace sales gross, OpenAI's figures here are net of partners, and Anthropic's latest point is a quarterly average, so today's combined figure is conservative. Hours saved are self-reported. Revenue is not job loss, and the wage bill leaves out the self-employed and occupations outside the 98 covered.
